intro: A compound verb is a verb's masu-stem plus a second verb that adds a direction: 飛ぶ + 込む = jump in, 飛ぶ + 出す = jump out, 持つ + 上げる = lift up. Each second verb keeps its spatial picture (into, out of, up) and stretches it to one abstract meaning: 込む goes deep inside, 出す bursts out or suddenly starts, 上げる / 上がる reaches the top, which means finished. Only the second verb conjugates, so choose by asking which way the action moves.

skills.rule: Stem + 込む means the action goes into something: into a space, into an organisation (申し込む), or deep into the mind (思い込む, 落ち込む).
skills.explain:
Literal use: the movement ends inside a pool, a room, a bag or a plane. 飛び込む (jump in), 持ち込む (bring in), 入り込む (get into), 書き込む (write into a form). The place you go into takes に: プールに飛び込む, 機内に持ち込む.

Figurative use: the action goes deep or stays fixed. 思い込む is to become convinced of something, usually wrongly; 落ち込む is to feel down; 考え込む is to sink into thought; 話し込む is to get absorbed in a long talk. 申し込む (apply, sign up) is pushing your name into an organisation: 講座に申し込む.

The edge: 込む is about going in or staying in. If the action comes out or starts suddenly, use 出す; if it goes up or gets finished, use 上げる. 込む is a godan verb: 込みます, 込んだ, 込んで.
patterns: [place] に [stem] 込む (飛び込む, 持ち込む)
[stem] 込んでいる (落ち込んでいる, 思い込んでいる): an ongoing inner state

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもたちがプールに{飛[と]び込[こ]んだ}。
examples.en: The children jumped into the pool.

examples.jp: 日本語[にほんご]の授業[じゅぎょう]に{申[もう]し込[こ]みました}。
examples.en: I signed up for the Japanese class.

examples.jp: 飛行機[ひこうき]に水[みず]は{持[も]ち込[こ]めません}。
examples.en: You can't take water onto the plane.

examples.jp: 試験[しけん]に落[お]ちて、兄[あに]はすっかり{落[お]ち込[こ]んで}いる。
examples.en: My brother failed the exam and is really down.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は自分[じぶん]が正[ただ]しいと{思[おも]い込[こ]んで}いる。
examples.en: He is convinced that he is right.

contrast.note: Opposite direction. 部屋に飛び込んだ: rushed into the room. 部屋から飛び出した: rushed out of the room. Watch the particle: に (into) goes with 込む, から (out of) with 出す.
合う means doing it together, 込む means going deep. 二人で話し合った: the two discussed it. 夜中まで話し込んだ: we got absorbed in talk until midnight.

mistakes.bad: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]を見[み]て、とても{落[お]ちました}。
mistakes.good: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]を見[み]て、とても{落[お]ち込[こ]みました}。
mistakes.note: 落ちる alone means fall or fail. Feeling down is 落ち込む.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]だと{思[おも]い込[こ]みます}。
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]だと{思[おも]います}。
mistakes.note: 思い込む is not a stronger 'think': it means being firmly, usually wrongly, convinced, and it is mostly used as 思い込んでいた / 思い込んでいる.

skills.tip: Can you add 'into' or 'deep in' to the English (jump into, sign into a course, sink into gloom)? Then it is 込む.

skills.rule: Stem + 出す means the action comes out (取り出す, 飛び出す, 思い出す) or suddenly breaks out (泣き出す, 走り出す, 降り出す).
skills.explain:
Out: something moves from inside to outside. 取り出す (take out), 飛び出す (rush out), 引き出す (withdraw money, draw out), 持ち出す (take out of a place). 思い出す is bringing something out of memory: it is English 'remember' in the sense of recall. The place left takes から: かばんから取り出す.

Sudden start: with verbs of crying, laughing, running, raining, 出す means the action bursts out without warning: 赤ちゃんが泣き出した, 雨が降り出した. It describes an unplanned onset, usually one you observe.

The edge with 始める: 始める is the neutral 'start' and works for planned actions, your own intentions and requests: 今から勉強し始めます, 食べ始めましょう. 出す is wrong there. Note that 飛び出す is intransitive even though 出す alone is transitive.
patterns: [place] から [thing] を 取り出す / 持ち出す
[place] に / から 飛び出す
[subject] が (急に) 泣き出す / 走り出す / 降り出す

examples.jp: かばんから財布[さいふ]を{取[と]り出[だ]した}。
examples.en: I took my wallet out of my bag.

examples.jp: この歌[うた]を聞[き]くと、学生[がくせい]時代[じだい]を{思[おも]い出[だ]します}。
examples.en: When I hear this song, I remember my student days.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもが急[きゅう]に道[みち]に{飛[と]び出[だ]して}きた。
examples.en: A child suddenly ran out into the road.

examples.jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんが急[きゅう]に{泣[な]き出[だ]した}。
examples.en: The baby suddenly burst into tears.

examples.jp: 出[で]かけようとしたら、雨[あめ]が{降[ふ]り出[だ]した}。
examples.en: Just as I was about to go out, it started to rain.

contrast.note: 始める is neutral and can be planned: 九時に読み始めましょう. 出す is a sudden, unplanned onset, so 読み出しましょう is wrong as 'let's start reading'.
Opposite direction: 外に飛び出す (rush out) against 中に飛び込む (rush in).
取り出す takes something out of a container; 取り上げる picks it up, takes it away from someone, or takes up a topic.

mistakes.bad: では、みんなで{食[た]べ出[だ]しましょう}。
mistakes.good: では、みんなで{食[た]べ始[はじ]めましょう}。
mistakes.note: The sudden-start 出す cannot be used for a plan or a suggestion. Use 始める.

mistakes.bad: 古[ふる]い写真[しゃしん]を見[み]て、子[こ]どものころを{覚[おぼ]えました}。
mistakes.good: 古[ふる]い写真[しゃしん]を見[み]て、子[こ]どものころを{思[おも]い出[だ]しました}。
mistakes.note: 覚える is to memorise or learn. Remembering something you had forgotten, or recalling the past, is 思い出す.

skills.tip: English 'out' or 'burst into ...ing'? 出す. A calm, planned 'start'? 始める.

skills.rule: Stem + 上げる / 上がる means up, or up to completion; use 上げる when someone does it to a thing (を), 上がる when the person or thing itself rises or gets done (が).
skills.explain:
Up: 持ち上げる (lift), 取り上げる (pick up), 立ち上がる (stand up), 起き上がる (sit up, get up from lying). Completion: the work reaches its top, so it is finished and ready: 仕上げる (finish off), 書き上げる (finish writing), 出来上がる (be ready, be completed).

上げる is transitive and needs を: レポートを仕上げる, 箱を持ち上げる. 上がる is intransitive and takes が: 料理が出来上がる, 彼が立ち上がる. Pairs exist: 仕上げる / 仕上がる. There is no 出来上げる, and 立ち上げる is a different verb (launch a project, start up a computer).

取り上げる has three common senses: pick up, take away from someone (often in the passive: 携帯を取り上げられた), and take up as a topic (ニュースで取り上げる). For 'used up, to the very end' use 切る (使い切る), not 上げる.
patterns: [thing] を 持ち上げる / 取り上げる
[work] を 仕上げる / 書き上げる
[work / dish] が 出来上がる / 仕上がる
[person] が 立ち上がる / 起き上がる

examples.jp: この箱[はこ]は重[おも]くて、一人[ひとり]では{持[も]ち上[あ]げられない}。
examples.en: This box is so heavy I can't lift it on my own.

examples.jp: 名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]ばれて、彼女[かのじょ]は{立[た]ち上[あ]がった}。
examples.en: When her name was called, she stood up.

examples.jp: 料理[りょうり]が{出来上[できあ]がりました}。
週末[しゅうまつ]までにレポートを{仕上[しあ]げて}ください。
examples.en: Please finish the report by the weekend.

examples.jp: 授業中[じゅぎょうちゅう]に携帯[けいたい]を使[つか]って、先生[せんせい]に{取[と]り上[あ]げられた}。
examples.en: I used my phone in class and the teacher took it away.

contrast.note: 上げる finishes a product (論文を書き上げた: the paper is written). 切る exhausts or goes to the very end (お金を使い切った: no money left).
Opposite direction: 取り上げる (take up, take away) against 取り下げる (withdraw a request or complaint).
取り上げる lifts or confiscates; 取り出す takes something out of a container.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]が入[はい]ってきて、学生[がくせい]はみんな{立[た]ち上[あ]げた}。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]が入[はい]ってきて、学生[がくせい]はみんな{立[た]ち上[あ]がった}。
mistakes.note: The students rise themselves, so it is intransitive 上がる. 立ち上げる means launching a project or a computer.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]、レポートを{仕上[しあ]がった}。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]の夜[よる]、レポートを{仕上[しあ]げた}。
mistakes.note: With を and a doer, use transitive 上げる. 上がる takes が: レポートが仕上がった.

skills.tip: Up or done? Then 上. Look at the particle: を before it means 上げる, が means 上がる.
